newsitem.title: USA: Continental files for Heathrow access.
newsitem.headline: Continental files for Heathrow access.

text.p: Continental Airlines Inc said Wednesday it filed with the U.S. Department of Transportation a proposed schedule for service between London Heathrow Airport and its three primary hubs in Newark, Houston and Cleveland.

When Heathrow access is made available, Continental said it seeks to operate six Heathrow flights a day at Newark, three at Houston and one at Cleveland, as well as maintaining existing service between Gatwick Airport and both Newark and Houston.
Continental also urged the DOT not to "waste time investigating the proposed American-British Airways deal until the U.K. agrees to open access to Heathrow."

"Without opening access to Heathrow first, any investigation of the American-British Airways deal must conclude the deal is so anti-competitive it could not be seriously considered," said Barry Simon, Continental's senior vice president for Europe.

Continental and other rival carriers have been outspoken opponents of the proposed alliance between AMR Corp's American Airlines and British Airways Plc, saying the deal is anti-competitive unless "meaningful" access to Heathrow Airport is available to assure competition.
